IGRP_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=

# IGRP Auth Issuer - Base URL of your authorization server (without trailing slash)
# The framework appends /.well-known/openid-configuration for OIDC discovery
# Example: http://auth.example.com (discovery at http://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration)
# or something like http://auth.example.com/igrp-access-management
IGRP_AUTH_ISSUER=

# IGRP Auth Scopes - Space-separated list of OAuth2 scopes to request.
# Must match scopes registered on the OAuth client AND advertised by the IdP.
# IGRP's discovery doc advertises `scopes_supported: ["openid", "email"]`.
# Requesting scopes beyond this (e.g. `profile`) is either silently dropped or
# rejected per Spring Authorization Server config. Register additional scopes
# on the client first. Defaults to "openid" if not set.
IGRP_AUTH_SCOPES=openid email

# Two URIs must be registered on your authorization server (BOTH are required —
# missing either causes silent failures: login loops back to /login, or logout
# leaves the IdP SSO session active even though local cookies were cleared).
#
# With NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH unset:
#   - OAuth callback URI:    http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/igrp-auth
#   - Post-logout redirect:  http://localhost:3000/login
#
# With NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH=/apps/template (the demo-v1 default):
#   - OAuth callback URI:    http://localhost:3000/apps/template/api/auth/callback/igrp-auth
#   - Post-logout redirect:  http://localhost:3000/apps/template/login
#
# Both must be configured on the client (e.g. `igrp-access-management` in IGRP
# Access Management). The OIDC spec requires byte-for-byte match.
#
# The IGRP provider enables PKCE (RFC 7636, S256) and OIDC `nonce` on the
# authorization-code exchange. No client-side configuration is required, but
# NEXTAUTH_URL, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, and the reverse-proxy path must remain
# stable across the /authorize → /callback round-trip — the PKCE/state/nonce
# cookies are JWE-encrypted with NEXTAUTH_SECRET and scoped to the
# NEXTAUTH_URL path. Mismatches surface as PKCE_ERROR / OAUTH_CALLBACK_ERROR
# at the callback step rather than as IdP-side rejections.

# ============================================
# NextAuth Configuration
# ============================================
# NextAuth URL — NextAuth treats this as the URL of its API ROOT, not the app root.
# It MUST include `/api/auth`, and when NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH is set it MUST also
# include the basePath. Getting this wrong produces a login loop with a growing
# nested ?callbackUrl=…?callbackUrl=… chain.
#   With NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH unset:           http://localhost:3000/api/auth
#   With NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH=/apps/template:  http://localhost:3000/apps/template/api/auth
NEXTAUTH_URL=

# NextAuth Secret - A random secret string used to encrypt JWT tokens and cookies
# Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 32
# Or use: https://generate-secret.vercel.app/32
NEXTAUTH_SECRET=

# NextAuth Internal URL - Internal URL for server-to-server communication
# Usually same as NEXTAUTH_URL, but can be different in Docker/K8s environments
# Example: http://localhost:3000 (for local) or http://nextjs-service:3000 (for K8s)
NEXTAUTH_URL_INTERNAL=

# Optional NextAuth session-cookie lifetime (seconds). Align to your IdP's
# refresh-token lifetime so the session cookie expires with the refresh token
# instead of NextAuth's ~30-day default. Leave unset to keep the default.
# IGRP_SESSION_MAX_AGE=28800

# Client session-poll interval, in seconds (how often the browser re-reads
# /api/auth/session; only a poll can persist a rotated token, because RSC
# renders cannot write cookies).
#
# HARD CEILING: this MUST be below 60s — the framework's proactive-refresh
# buffer (TOKEN_REFRESH_BUFFER_MS in @igrp/framework-next-auth). The jwt
# callback only refreshes once the access token is within 60s of expiry, so a
# poll slower than that never lands inside the refresh window: the refreshes
# that do run happen in read-only RSC context and cannot write the cookie, and
# the session dies in a gap the user sees as a random bounce to /login.
# withIGRPAuth warns in development when this value is 60 or above.
#
# 45 leaves ~15s of margin for jitter and request duration, and works for any
# access-token lifetime above ~60s. Lower it further only if your IdP issues
# very short-lived access tokens.
# Unset / non-numeric / <= 0 falls back to 180 (framework default) — which is
# itself above the ceiling, so set it explicitly.
IGRP_SESSION_REFETCH_INTERVAL=45

# ============================================
# IGRP Framework Configuration
# ============================================
# IGRP Access Manager API - Base URL for the IGRP App Manager API
# Example: https://api.example.com/igrp-manager
IGRP_ACCESS_MANAGEMENT_API=

# IGRP App Code - Unique identifier for your application in the IGRP framework
# Example: demo-app | DEMO_APP | APP-DEMO
IGRP_APP_CODE=

# Client-readable copy of IGRP_APP_CODE — the logout / teardown loading screens
# render it client-side, where the server-only IGRP_APP_CODE is not available.
# Set this to the same value as IGRP_APP_CODE.
NEXT_PUBLIC_IGRP_APP_CODE=

# IGRP Preview Mode - Enable preview mode to skip authentication checks
# Set to true to disable authentication (useful for development/demo)
# Set to false or leave empty to enable authentication
# Values: true or false (case-insensitive, handles quotes)
IGRP_PREVIEW_MODE=

# Enable Access Management synchronization
# When set to true, the framework syncs the application, resources/routes,
# and on-code menus with the IGRP Access Management API at startup. Sync is
# scheduled post-response via `after()` so it never blocks the first request.
# Values: true or false
IGRP_SYNC_ACCESS=

# Enable on-code menus synchronization
# When set to true, the framework pushes `src/temp/menus/menus.ts`
# (IGRP_DEFAULT_MENU) to Access Management at startup via
# syncApplicationMenus. Requires IGRP_SYNC_ACCESS=true and
# IGRP_PREVIEW_MODE=false to take effect.
# When false (default), AM remains the source of truth and no push happens.
# NOTE: enabling this overwrites the menus on the AM side with the local array.
# Values: true or false
IGRP_SYNC_ON_CODE_MENUS=false

# Sync menu<->role assignments during the on-code menu push
# Forwarded as the `syncRoles` argument of syncApplicationMenus. When true,
# Access Management also reconciles the menu role assignments; when false,
# only the menu entries are synced and existing role assignments are kept.
# Only consulted when IGRP_SYNC_ON_CODE_MENUS=true and the push actually runs.
# When unset, defaults to true (the AM client default) — set to false to opt out.
# Values: true or false
IGRP_SYNC_ON_CODE_MENU_ROLES=true

# Enable permissions catalog synchronization
# When set to true, the framework pushes the catalog declared in
# `.igrpstudio/permissions.json` (maintained by iGRP Studio) to Access
# Management at startup via syncPermissions. Requires IGRP_SYNC_ACCESS=true and
# IGRP_PREVIEW_MODE=false to take effect.
# When false (default), AM remains the source of truth and no push happens.
# NOTE: the sync is an idempotent upsert keyed on `name` — permissions removed
# from the JSON are NOT deleted in AM (that would break tokens already granting
# them); retire them via the AM admin UI.
# NOTE: registering a permission does not make it checkable — AM must still
# grant it to a role and the user's token must carry the claim. See
# docs/PERMISSIONS.md.
# Values: true or false
IGRP_SYNC_PERMISSIONS=false

## ============================================
# Access Management API authentication
##
## When IGRP_SYNC_ACCESS=true, the framework authenticates to the Access
## Management API using OAuth2 `client_credentials`:
##   1. POST {IGRP_ACCESS_MANAGEMENT_API}/oauth2/token
##      Authorization: Basic base64(IGRP_M2M_CLIENT_ID:IGRP_M2M_CLIENT_SECRET)
##      grant_type=client_credentials
##   2. The returned bearer token is cached until expiry and refreshed
##      transparently. One token is shared across all sync calls.
##
## Identity headers (IGRP_SERVICE_ID) are sent as `X-Machine-Service-ID`.
##
## All four variables (IGRP_SERVICE_ID, IGRP_M2M_CLIENT_ID,
## IGRP_M2M_CLIENT_SECRET, IGRP_ACCESS_MANAGEMENT_API) are validated at
## render time when IGRP_SYNC_ACCESS=true and IGRP_PREVIEW_MODE=false.
## Misconfiguration shows up as IgrpConfigError in `global-error.tsx`
## rather than an opaque 4xx from the AM server.
## ============================================

# Service identity — used as the resource name on the Access Management
# server and sent as the X-Machine-Service-ID header. Must be a non-empty
# identifier (lowercase alphanumeric + dashes/underscores, 2-64 chars).
# Example: demo-igrp
IGRP_SERVICE_ID=

# OAuth2 client_credentials — client identifier issued by the Access
# Management admin for this application's M2M integration.
# Example: igrp-m2m-client-id-1234
IGRP_M2M_CLIENT_ID=

# OAuth2 client_credentials — client secret paired with IGRP_M2M_CLIENT_ID.
# Server-only; never exposed to the browser. Rotate via your AM admin.
# Example: igrp-m2m-client-secret-1234
IGRP_M2M_CLIENT_SECRET=

# Used for app switching functionality

NEXT_IGRP_APP_CENTER_URL=

# Next Public Base Path - Base path for the application (if deployed in a subdirectory)
# Leave empty if app is at root domain
# Example: /my-app (if app is at https://example.com/my-app)
NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH=

# Next Public IGRP App Home Slug - Default route to redirect after login

NEXT_PUBLIC_IGRP_APP_HOME_SLUG=

# Next Public Allowed Domains - Comma-separated list of allowed image domains
# Used for Next.js Image component remotePatterns configuration
# Example: example.com,cdn.example.com,images.example.com
NEXT_PUBLIC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=

# Next Public IGRP Profile URL if the apps-center is have is own url- Base URL for profile
# Used by the frontend user profile
# Example: https://frontend-igrp.example.com/profile
NEXT_PUBLIC_IGRP_PROFILE_URL=

# Next Public IGRP Notification URL if the apps-center is have is own url - Base URL for notification
# Used by the frontend

NEXT_PUBLIC_IGRP_NOTIFICATION_URL=

# Next Public IGRP Settings URL if the apps-center is have is own url - Base URL for settings

NEXT_PUBLIC_IGRP_SETTINGS_URL=
